summary: A directly reviewed Registry capture of a user-posted X report shows ChatGPT being asked to rewrite prompt material while the user says “Again, do not touch image generator”; immediately below, the interface displays a Thinking/image-generation state. The accompanying post reports that mentioning “art”, “prompt”, or “image” repeatedly caused the image generator to fire, forced app reloads, switched the visible model from GPT-5.5 to “5.4 Thinking”, and that uploading an image without follow-up text could activate generation or crash the app. The capture does not establish the internal cause of the behaviour or its prevalence.

taxonomy_classification.classification_basis: Direct Registry-artefact review supports two provisional failure mechanisms. Primary VIGIL-FC-000003 Target and Scope Authority Transposition is supported because the user authorised prompt rewriting/discussion while explicitly withholding image-generation authority, yet the interface entered the image-generation path. Secondary VIGIL-FC-000078 Continuity-State Validity Failure is supported because the corrective wording “Again, do not touch image generator”, the report that the generator fires whenever relevant terms are mentioned, and the repeated reload requirement together indicate that an unwanted image-generation trajectory remains or re-enters governing continuation despite evidence that it is no longer valid for the user's task. Confidence for both mappings is medium: the screenshot is a user-posted partial interaction and cannot fully distinguish inherited sticky state from repeated lexical re-triggering. VIGIL-FC-000002, VIGIL-FC-000040 and VIGIL-FC-000043 remain rejected for the previously recorded boundary reasons.

primary_classification.classification_basis: The preserved screenshot directly shows an authorised text-task scope, an explicit exclusion of image-generator use, and a subsequent displayed image-generation state. The observable governance failure is a transition into a materially different action scope without authority for that scope.

secondary_classifications.classification_basis: The preserved interaction includes the corrective instruction “Again, do not touch image generator”, while the accompanying report describes the generator repeatedly firing on relevant lexical cues and requiring reload recovery. This supports a sticky invalid interaction-state trajectory across conversational continuation. Confidence is medium because the partial artefact cannot fully distinguish inherited state from repeated re-triggering.

The repeated 'Again' corrective instruction, 'whenever' recurrence report and reload requirement support a provisional continuity-state interpretation, but the artefact does not fully distinguish inherited sticky state from repeated lexical re-triggering.
Capability-Authority Conflation remains rejected because the artefact does not show that technical capability or tool availability was used as the material basis for permission.

Unwarranted Control Activation remains rejected because the observed image-generation path is an action/tool-routing state, not an evidenced governance safeguard whose defined activation conditions were unsatisfied.

Control-State Preservation Failure remains rejected because that class concerns preservation of an already-operative governance control, whereas the sticky state at issue here is the continuation validity of an interaction/tool state.
vigil_assessment.factual_basis: The directly reviewed Registry capture preserves the user-posted X report and embedded ChatGPT interface screenshot. The screenshot visibly shows a request to rewrite prompt material together with the corrective instruction “Again, do not touch image generator”, followed by a displayed Thinking/image-generation state. The accompanying post reports repeated triggering around the words “art”, “prompt”, and “image”, app glitch/reload behaviour, a visible switch from GPT-5.5 to “5.4 Thinking”, and image-upload activation or crash behaviour without follow-up text. The partial capture does not establish the internal router, tool-selection mechanism, whether the unwanted state was inherited across turns or repeatedly re-triggered, or platform-wide prevalence.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: The occurrence engages both action-scope authority and continuity-state validity. First, permission to discuss or rewrite prompt text did not authorise a materially different image-generation action. Second, once the unwanted image-generation trajectory had emerged, the user's explicit corrective instruction should have invalidated or reset that trajectory for subsequent continuation. The fact that the captured interaction still enters the image-generation state, together with the report that this happened whenever relevant words were mentioned and required repeated reloads, supports a provisional Continuity-State Validity Failure analysis. The evidence remains insufficient to claim a specific router, memory or model-state implementation.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: INC-000009 illustrates a dual governance requirement for multimodal systems: action authority must remain bounded to the user's authorised scope, and interaction/tool state must remain validity-bounded across conversational continuation. An explicitly rejected mode should not remain governing merely because it was previously active, nor should lexical mentions silently reinstate it without renewed authority.

clauses.recovered_invariant_interpretation: A repeatedly invalidated tool state must not remain or re-enter the governing continuation state without a fresh valid basis; recurring lexical cues are not themselves sufficient to make the excluded action mode valid.
